claims.claim: Bandai Namco passed a resolution to dissolve and liquidate its subsidiary Reflector Entertainment.
Unknown 9: Awakening was Reflector Entertainment's one and only game.
Bandai Namco expects to post an extraordinary loss of 21 million euros as a result of the liquidation.
Unknown 9: Awakening was released on October 18, 2024.
A month after launch, Reflector laid off 18% of its workforce.
In January 2025, more layoffs followed as an in-development project was cancelled.
Reflector wrote on LinkedIn that Bandai Namco concluded it "could not justify several more years of investment" after reviewing a project in pre-production.
Bandai Namco acquired Reflector Entertainment in September 2020.
The closure was announced in November 2026, about six years after the acquisition.

issues.quote: Six years for one release is a slow way to spend 21 million euros.
issues.problem: The €21 million is the extraordinary loss Bandai Namco expects from the liquidation, not the amount spent on the studio over six years. The line reads as a wry aside, but it loosely conflates the two.

check.summary: All factual claims and on-screen figures are supported by the sources: the closure, the €21 million expected loss, the 18% layoff a month after launch, the LinkedIn quote, the September 2020 acquisition, the 18 October 2024 launch and the January 2025 project cancellation. Opinion lines are clearly framed as opinion. The only issue is a minor imprecision in the joke that treats the liquidation loss as money spent over six years.
